title: Piano players at Lula White's and Manuel Manetta
summary: Who played piano at Lula White's (Jelly Roll, others) and Garland's recollection of Manuel Manetta, now teaching.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Huh? Did you work there? No, nothing but piano. Yeah, I already telling people about he was there. He know much about Lula White as you do. I'm not telling you no story. He was out there in the country, pig and peas. I heard that woman come talking about, Ed used to go with her. I said, go with who? I said, Ed don't know Lula White if he's here. He used to go with her. George Lambert was old man, a big gambler. I had the gambling house on Cronlet, on St. Charles, between Petita and the foot of Petita, between Petita and Padres, upstairs. Big gambling house. I used to carry clothes there.
Who was the piano player at the Lula White? Who played there? Well, there were several different fellas.
That one time, Jelly Rolls played there, and then Albert Cal played there.
Did you ever hear of a guy whose name is Manuel Mineta? Manuel Mineta, sure. Do you know him?

Oh, yeah. Manuel Mineta played violin and piano. Played trumpet. He's teaching now. We saw him. We spent a lot of time with him. He's teaching music now. He's a little over in Algiers. That's right. I don't know Manuel. Call him horse.
A lot of people still call him horse.
Yeah. Did he play at Lulu's? He played down the district, yeah. He used to play, I think he played for Mimicristine down there on the basement between Conard and Bianbo.
